A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LGA research work, including the complete supplementary material. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original LGA benchmark results, component ablations, and qualitative analyses in Section 4, with additional experiments in supplementary Section 9.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, and supplementary experiments, including Tables 1–6 and 8 and the experimental figures.

M1.justification: Action anatomy, CLUSTER-Segment, multimodal fusion, matching, and training objectives are unchanged. Figure 2 corrects an encoder label to match the existing caption and method description; it does not establish an architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HMDB51, Kinetics, UCF101, SSv2-Small, and SSv2-Full. The supplementary evaluation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmark, matching and segmentation comparisons, VLM experiments, and supplementary Table 8. No evaluated baseline is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain the same splits, CLIP-initialized ViT-B/16 configuration, eight-frame default, preprocessing, and 10,000-episode evaluation. Supplementary shot-count, frame-count, and N-way protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component, fusion, matching, segmentation, and atomic-action-count ablations are identical. The VLM comparisons, feature visualizations, description examples, and supplementary sensitivity analyses are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same average-accuracy procedure over 10,000 test episodes. There are no changes to seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged across the main text and supplement. For example, Table 1 retains LGA's HMDB51 accuracies of 86.8% and 89.3% under the same 1-shot and 5-shot settings.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and mathematical definitions, including fusion and AB-MHM matching in Equations 1–5, are identical. Neither version adds or revises theoretical assumptions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about atomic action representations, multimodal fusion and matching, and performance across five benchmarks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality complementarity, dataset-dependent benefits, and lower-shot improvements are unchanged. Both retain the discussion of excessive segmentation, LLM hallucinations, and visual-textual misalignment.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures are identical, including GPT-4o prompt design, VLM prompts, training details, and dataset-specific hyperparameters in Table 7. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier FSAR methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Figure 2 replaces the video encoder's wording 'Textual Backbone' with 'Visual Backbone', and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The prose, headings, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 receives a localized correction to its video-encoder label. No figures or tables are added, removed, or relocated, and the remaining displays and page layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 2's video encoder from 'Textual Backbone' to 'Visual Backbone' removes a misleading modality label and aligns the architecture diagram with its existing caption and method description. This provides a limited clarity improvement; the scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged.
